name: sky
title: The sky over the valley: aurora and space weather

sources.name: swpc_ovation
sources.license: public domain (US government work; no explicit statement)
sources.credit: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center (OVATION Prime)

sources.name: swpc_kp_1m
sources.license: public domain (US government work; no explicit statement)

storage: No tables of its own and no archive files: rows in core's raw.record only. OVATION: one row per snapshot every 30 min (651 values; the payload is about 0.5 KB after Postgres compresses it on a quiet day, about 1.5 KB when the oval is busy), about 40-90 KB a day with the row and its indexes. Kp: one row per UTC hour (60 values, about 0.8 KB), about 25 KB a day. Downloads: about 7 MB a day (OVATION's global file is about 145 KB gzipped; Kp about 1.3 KB).
ethics: Nature, not people: no personal data. US government data from services.swpc.noaa.gov, whose robots.txt returns 404 (no rules); one request per source per run, at least 2 s apart, with our User-Agent. OVATION's values are the chance of aurora overhead, not of seeing it from the valley: anything shown from them must say so and stay approximate (docs/sources/sky.md).
